text: Payroll on Friday. Rent on the first. An invoice next week.
Hodd is a treasury on Arc that keeps money ahead of what it owes.
Hodd reads your wallet's live USDC on Arc Testnet, and the bills you enter.
The Treasury Engine protects every bill inside your lead time,
from 3 to 30 days, plus a safety buffer.
Only what is left is deployable.
No language model calculates an amount.
Autopilot runs from a vault contract.
The owner's wallet owns it; Hodd's Circle agent wallet is only its operator.
This owner funded Autopilot with 30 USDC from their own wallet.
The contract allows Morpho, Hodd's USYC pool,
one approved recipient capped at 7 USDC, and the owner.
Anything else reverts. The owner can pause, or take everything back without Hodd.
On October 15, the engine proposed:
invest 10.52 USDC into Morpho, at a 4.20% recent yield.
The AI advisor, gpt-oss-120b on Groq, saw aggregate figures only,
and answered FOLLOW: higher yield, no pending bills.
It may follow, allocate, wait or move between strategies.
Bills never reach the model; answers outside its envelope are discarded.
Many runs end in no action, and the history records those too.
Before signing, the runner checks the decision against fresh balances.
The Circle agent wallet signed one call on the owner's vault: depositToStrategy.
Arc confirmed it. Hodd verified the receipt from the vault's own events, then marked the run complete.
Cash can also earn in Hodd's USYC pool, the one contract Circle allowlisted.
A 1 USDC round trip returned 0.999895 USDC.
Autopilot's USYC path was verified on a test vault; this account has used Morpho.
Hoddie answers from the engine's numbers.
Claude runs Hodd over MCP, with your approval.
Circle Gateway unifies USDC across 12 testnets, Arc included.
Hodd Finance.
Money should know when it will be needed.
